title: This Metal Melts in Your Hand at 86 Degrees (but Boils at 4,350)

scenes.text: This metal melts in your hand.
Gallium. Solid on the table. Hold it for a minute and it runs through your fingers like mercury.
It melts at 86 degrees Fahrenheit. Your body is 98.
But it won't boil until 4,350 degrees. That's one of the widest liquid ranges of any metal on Earth.
It expands when it freezes, like water, so it can even crack a glass bottle.
And it isn't toxic like mercury. Pour it out, let it set, melt it again.

description:
Gallium is a silvery metal that melts at just 29.8 degrees Celsius (about 86 Fahrenheit), so a lump of it turns to liquid in the warmth of your hand. Yet it does not boil until around 2,400 Celsius (4,350 Fahrenheit), one of the widest liquid ranges of any element.
Like water, it expands as it solidifies, by about 3 percent, which is why it is never stored in glass. Unlike mercury, its vapour is not toxic.
What is the strangest material you have ever held? Comment below.
first_comment: Gallium is also inside your phone: gallium arsenide and gallium nitride run LEDs, lasers and fast chips. Which element would you most like to hold?
